lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Coffee Roasters | Barista | Metro City, USA | Oct 2025 - Present
- Prepared drinks for the morning rush of about 200 orders and kept the bar stocked.
- Opened the café three days a week and handled the daily cash count.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: The résumé leaves an unaccounted period between the university web-development role and the internship.
items.because: The listed roles end in August 2024 and begin in June 2025, and the résumé does not explain the gap.

items.says: The Barista entry leads the experience section ahead of the technical experience.
The stocking detail does not show how it affected the rush.
“Prepared drinks” names a task but not a barista skill or technique.
“cafØ” is a corrupted spelling of “café.”
items.because: The corrupted character looks like a résumé typo and can distract the reader.

items.says: The opening and cash-counting responsibilities have no stated result.
“Handled” obscures the specific action taken on the cash count.
The 35% performance improvement does not name its metric or comparison.
items.because: Without a metric and baseline, the percentage is difficult to interpret.

items.says: The test result comes after the test-writing detail.
items.because: That makes the impact harder to scan.

items.says: React state does not prevent cross-site scripting when untrusted input is rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
items.because: React state does not sanitize input, and dangerouslySetInnerHTML parses it as HTML.

items.says: The XSS prevention claim has no stated verification result.
items.because: Without a test, audit, or other verification, the claim is harder to assess.

items.says: The load-time and booking results are buried after a long implementation setup.
“Owned” describes responsibility but not what you did with the websites or library.
items.because: It gives little evidence of your web-development contribution or technical work.

items.says: The ownership claim has no stated result.
“Other developers relied on” is a vague justification for the library.
The broken-page reduction appears after the interview detail.
items.because: That makes the result harder to scan.

items.says: The checklist description does not say what it covered.
“Search time” does not say what was timed.
items.because: Page response time and time to find a course describe different improvements.

items.says: The live-arrival detail does not say how the app obtains the data.
“Opened in 0.8s” does not define what counted as opening.
“Against 2.9s before” is an awkward, clipped comparison.
The React and TypeScript claim conflicts with the Vue stack in the heading.
items.because: A reader cannot tell which framework the project used or which stack you worked in.

items.says: “Worked on the frontend” is vague participation framing.
The booking-flow contribution has no stated result or benefit.
The calendar-component detail has no stated outcome.
The calendar-component bullet is not the opening bullet, though it is the stronger project accomplishment.
The travel-search bullet does not describe work on the Library Room Booking project.
items.because: It describes a travel-search rebuild whose results closely match the Lumen Travel internship bullet.

items.says: The travel-search results do not identify their measures or comparison points.
items.because: The load-time measure and the booking change’s baseline and period are unclear.

items.says: The impact is buried after the implementation detail.
items.because: The load-time and booking results are the bullet’s main outcomes.

items.says: “More than” and “about” soften the results and add wording.
items.because: Those qualifiers make the impact less direct and less precise.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled in Skills—Tools.
items.because: The misspelling can make a reader question the accuracy of the skills list.

items.says: Angular appears in Skills—Tools without a supporting role or project entry.
items.because: A reader cannot connect Angular to the described experience and may question your actual experience with it.
